label: LLM reasoning & agents
blurb: Test-time compute, RL fine-tuning, tool-using agents

profile.description: I study how large language models reason and act: test-time compute, RL fine-tuning for reasoning, and agents that use tools.

themes.name: Reasoning and test-time compute
themes.description: Methods that improve LLM reasoning at inference time: chain-of-thought, search over reasoning paths, self-verification, and scaling laws for test-time compute.

themes.name: RL fine-tuning of LLMs
themes.description: Reinforcement learning to train language models, including RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards, reward modeling, and the stability of policy-gradient methods for LLMs.

themes.name: Tool-using agents
themes.description: LLM agents that call tools, browse, or write code over many steps, and the benchmarks and environments used to evaluate them.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference
themes.description: Making LLM inference cheaper or faster: quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache compression, and efficient serving.

not_interested: Papers that only apply an off-the-shelf LLM to a domain task (law, medicine, education) without new methods
Computer vision papers unless they involve language-model reasoning

profile.description: I work on machine learning for small-molecule drug discovery and protein design.

themes.name: Structure-based virtual screening
themes.description: Docking, scoring functions, and ML models that rank compounds against a protein target, including benchmarks and analyses of why screening succeeds or fails.

themes.name: Generative molecular design
themes.description: Models that generate or optimize small molecules (diffusion, language models, RL) under property or binding constraints.

themes.name: Protein structure and design
themes.description: Predicting protein structures and complexes, and designing new proteins or binders with deep learning.

themes.name: Molecular property prediction
themes.description: Predicting ADMET, solubility, or activity from molecular structure, especially with graph neural networks or foundation models.

not_interested: Materials science papers without biological targets
General graph neural network papers not applied to molecules

profile.description: I work on learning-based robot manipulation.

themes.name: Vision-language-action models
themes.description: Large pretrained policies that map images and language instructions to robot actions, and how to train, fine-tune, or evaluate them.

themes.name: Imitation learning
themes.description: Learning manipulation policies from human or teleoperated demonstrations, including diffusion policies and data collection systems.

themes.name: Sim-to-real reinforcement learning
themes.description: Training robot policies with RL in simulation and transferring them to real hardware.

themes.name: Dexterous manipulation
themes.description: Multi-fingered hands and contact-rich tasks such as in-hand reorientation and tool use.

profile.description: I develop computational methods for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.

themes.name: Single-cell foundation models
themes.description: Large pretrained models of single-cell gene expression, how they are trained, and evaluations of whether they beat simple baselines.

themes.name: Spatial transcriptomics methods
themes.description: Computational methods for spatially resolved transcriptomics: cell segmentation, deconvolution, spatial domains, and cell-cell communication.

themes.name: Perturbation modeling
themes.description: Predicting the effects of genetic or chemical perturbations on cells, including Perturb-seq analysis and in-silico perturbation models.

label: Computational neuroscience
blurb: Neural dynamics, learning rules, brain-like models

profile.description: I study neural computation with models and data.

themes.name: Neural population dynamics
themes.description: Low-dimensional dynamics and latent-variable models of recorded neural populations.

themes.name: Biologically plausible learning
themes.description: Learning rules that could run in the brain, such as alternatives to backpropagation and synaptic plasticity models.

themes.name: Deep networks as brain models
themes.description: Comparing artificial neural networks with neural or behavioral data to test hypotheses about the brain.

not_interested: Clinical neurology and brain imaging diagnostics
Spiking network papers aimed only at efficiency
